quote: We introduce empirical support dynamics, a framework that quantifies how RLVR preserves, expands, and shrinks access to verified solutions.
supports: The paper's framework, empirical support dynamics, measures question by question how RLVR preserves, expands and shrinks access to verified solutions.

quote: empirical support: the set of questions on which a model produces at least one verified success under a specified sampling budget and evaluation protocol
supports: Empirical support is the set of questions with at least one verified success at a stated sampling budget and evaluation protocol.

quote: With finite logits, an unmasked softmax gives positive probability to every token and hence every finite completion permitted by the generation rules.
supports: v5 grants that exact support is never empty under a softmax, so its claims concern practical (observed) access, not exact support.

quote: We refer to this movement from negligible toward observable probability as empirical support diffusion.
supports: Training that lifts a correct completion from negligible to observable probability is called empirical support diffusion.

quote: Pairing whether each model produces at least one verified success yields preservation, shrinkage, expansion, and out of support.
supports: Each question is classed as preservation, shrinkage, expansion or out of support from paired success at a fixed budget, decoding and verifier.

quote: these findings reveal an “invisible leash” in current RLVR practice: it can make existing successes more reliable while losing access to other verified solutions
supports: The 'invisible leash': current RLVR makes existing successes more reliable while losing access to other verified solutions.

quote: the shrinkage of observed support outweighs its expansion: more questions lose a verified success than gain one at the stated sampling budgets
supports: In every evaluated model-level aggregate, more questions lose a verified success than gain one.

quote: We adopt ProRL-1.5B-v1 (Liu et al., 2025a) as our main RLVR method due to its robust long-horizon training framework.
supports: The main RLVR model is ProRL-1.5B-v1 (Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B, from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B).

quote: We additionally include ProRL-1.5B-v2 as a separate checkpoint for comparison (Tab. 1).
supports: ProRL-1.5B-v2 is evaluated as a separate checkpoint and reported only in the Table 1 aggregates.

quote: we evaluate other RLVR variants at multiple scales (7B–14B parameters), including Skywork (Wei et al., 2023), AceReason-Nemotron (Chen et al., 2025a)
supports: Other evaluated RLVR models are 7B-14B: Skywork-OR1, AceReason-Nemotron and Phi4-Reason, plus one vision-language model.

quote: In Reasoning Gym, we especially focus on tasks that ProRL explicitly highlighted as challenging for the base model.
supports: The Reasoning Gym tasks are those ProRL itself highlighted as hard for the base model.

quote: Sampling budgets are k\in\{4096,8192\} for the 1.5B–14B math comparisons, k\in\{1024,2048,4096,8192,16384\} for Reasoning Gym, and k\in\{1024,2048\} for other non-math datasets.
supports: Budgets are k 4,096 or 8,192 on math, up to 16,384 on Reasoning Gym and 1,024 or 2,048 on other non-math sets.

quote: The OLMo, SFT/DAPO, and training-checkpoint comparisons use k=256
supports: The OLMo, SFT-versus-DAPO and training-checkpoint comparisons use k = 256.

quote: We compare checkpoints at matched sampling budgets and decoding settings using the same benchmark acceptance criterion.
supports: Both checkpoints are compared at matched budgets and decoding settings under the same acceptance criterion.

quote: For all models, we utilized a sampling temperature of 0.6 , a top\_p value of 0.95 , and a maximum response length of 32768 tokens.
supports: All models are sampled at temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, with a 32,768-token response limit.
ProRL-1.5B-v1 overall: P 2,400, E 36, S 163, O 805, NSCR -0.05.
ProRL-1.5B-v2 overall: P 2,388, E 48, S 175, O 793, NSCR -0.05.

quote: ProRL-1.5B-v2 solves 48 questions on which the base model produces no verified success at the evaluation budget: 39 non-math and 9 math questions
supports: ProRL-1.5B-v2's 48 expansion questions are 39 non-math and 9 math.

quote: ProRL-1.5B-v2 loses 175 questions while gaining 48, a ratio of approximately 3.6{:}1
supports: ProRL-1.5B-v2 loses about 3.6 questions for every one it gains.

quote: newly solved questions make up at most 2\% of RLVR successes
supports: Across the six 1.5B-14B comparisons, expansions are at most 2 % of the RL model's successes (NDR <= 0.02).
Table 6 (ProRL-1.5B-v1 vs base) gives the non-math aggregate as P 1,045, E 31, S 107, O 674, the counts of Table 1's non-math row.

quote: Non-Math Reasoning Benchmarks (pass@2048)
supports: ProRL-1.5B-v1's non-math rows (SimpleQA, LiveBench, SciBench, LiveCodeBench) are read at k = 2,048.

quote: The high-budget deficit also appears on AIME2024, where base pass@8192 reaches 93.3\% , compared with ProRL-1.5B-v1’s 83.3\%
supports: On AIME 2024 at k = 8,192 the base reaches 93.3 % against ProRL-1.5B-v1's 83.3 %.

quote: ProRL-1.5B-v1 also retains a coverage advantage on arc_1d, boxnet, and graph_color_vertex20 through the largest sampling budget shown (Fig. 3).
supports: The Reasoning Gym expansion curves compare ProRL-1.5B-v1 with its base; ProRL keeps its lead on arc_1d, boxnet and graph_color_vertex20 at the largest budget shown.
boxnet at k = 16,384: base (R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) 0.345, ProRL-1.5B-v1 0.492.
At k = 1 (base / ProRL): arc_1d 0.010 / 0.040, boxnet 0.024 / 0.097, graph_color_vertex20 0.000 / 0.881.
At k = 2,048 (base / ProRL): arc_1d 0.570 / 0.680 (its largest budget), boxnet 0.289 / 0.437, graph_color_vertex20 0.762 / 1.000.
At k = 4,096 (base / ProRL): boxnet 0.308 / 0.443, graph_color_vertex20 0.901 / 1.000 (its largest budget).

quote: at 1,024 attempts, the base model reaches 40\% while ProRL reaches only 30\%
supports: On leg_counting the base overtakes ProRL at k = 1,024 (40 % vs 30 %) after ProRL led at k = 1 (28 % vs 4 %).
At k = 1,024 (base / ProRL): leg_counting 0.400 / 0.300, family_relationships 1.000 / 0.880, power_function 1.000 / 0.901.
At k = 1 (base / ProRL): dice 0.000 / 0.180, prime_factorization_hard 0.832 / 1.000, palindrome_generation 0.154 / 0.923.
On dice the base reaches full coverage (1.000) at k = 8,192, as ProRL does.

quote: while the base model catches up as k grows. Both models reach full coverage at the largest displayed budgets.
supports: On the nine preservation tasks the base catches up as k grows and both models reach full coverage.

quote: Evaluating the base model on Reasoning Gym revealed frequent mismatches between its answer format and the verifier’s expected input.
supports: The base model's Reasoning Gym answers often did not match the verifier's expected format.

quote: ProRL, which was trained on Reasoning Gym data, generally followed the expected format.
supports: ProRL, trained on Reasoning Gym data, generally followed the expected format.

quote: We therefore clarified the format instructions in the prompts and expanded answer extraction to recognize alternative representations.
supports: The authors clarified the prompts' format instructions and widened answer extraction to accept alternative representations.

quote: These changes distinguish our evaluation protocol from the one used to report ProRL’s original Reasoning Gym scores.
supports: The format-tolerant protocol differs from the one behind ProRL's own Reasoning Gym scores.

quote: Our core answer-processing pipeline applies to both models, with additional steps designed primarily to address format compatibility issues commonly encountered in base-model responses.
supports: The core answer processing is shared; extra task-specific steps target base-model formats.

quote: For base models only, we convert ground truth fractions from a/b format to LaTeX format \frac{a}{b}
supports: On dice the ground-truth fraction is converted to LaTeX for base models only.

quote: As a final fallback, the system extracts content following </think> tags when all previous methods fail
supports: The last extraction fallback takes the text after the </think> tag.

quote: We implement comprehensive cleaning of the JSON format to meet these evaluation requirements.
supports: boxnet answers are cleaned (markdown wrappers removed, single dicts listed, nested values flattened) before verification.

quote: RLVR can improve verified success by making otherwise useful responses conform more reliably to the required format.
supports: One hypothesis for the remaining expansion: RLVR makes otherwise useful answers conform to the verifier's format.

quote: We measure expansion after applying these answer-processing rules.
supports: The reported expansion is measured after the format-tolerant processing.

quote: Under this hypothesis, expansion arises from improved coordination of partially reliable subskills.
supports: A second hypothesis: expansion comes from reliably composing partially reliable subskills.

quote: RLVR makes correct answers much easier to obtain on questions already within the base model’s reach.
supports: RLVR's main effect is precision: correct answers become easier to sample on questions the base can already solve.

quote: For ProRL, average accuracy rises from 54.5\% to 65.4\% as answer entropy falls from 1.30 to 0.66
supports: For ProRL, avg@32 accuracy rises from 54.5 % to 65.4 % while final-answer entropy falls from 1.30 to 0.66.

quote: ProRL’s average token entropy rises from 0.44 to 0.52
supports: ProRL's average token-level entropy rises (0.44 to 0.52).

quote: By contrast, both AceReason models and Skywork reduce entropy at both levels relative to their reference checkpoints.
supports: AceReason and Skywork lower both token-level and answer-level entropy.

quote: Training-stage analysis shows that expansion can be temporary: AIME25 and Minerva gain coverage at intermediate checkpoints but end below their initial coverage.
supports: Along a DAPO run (R1-Distill-1.5B, to step 300, k 256), expansion on AIME25 and Minerva appears at intermediate checkpoints and is lost by the end.

quote: On Olympiad, gains decrease from 13 at step 30 to 5 at step 300, while losses increase from 22 to 61.
supports: On OlympiadBench, gains shrink from 13 to 5 and losses grow from 22 to 61 between steps 30 and 300.

quote: SFT maintains or increases total coverage on all six benchmarks (nonnegative NSCR), whereas DAPO produces net shrinkage on four.
supports: From Qwen2.5-Math-7B on DeepMath-103K at k 256, SFT never loses net coverage while DAPO shrinks on four of six benchmarks.

quote: Support dynamics metrics and pass@256 performance of OLMo-2-0425-1B-DPO vs RLVR.
supports: The OLMo comparison is a DPO checkpoint against its RLVR successor, at k = 256.
OLMo-2-0425-1B (DPO to RLVR), math: P 761, E 83, S 104, O 599, NDR 0.10, NSCR -0.02.

quote: Its 83 gains still fall short of 104 losses, however, so its higher SDS coexists with negative NSCR.
supports: OLMo-2-1B has the highest discovery but its 83 gains are below its 104 losses.

quote: In every reported shrinkage comparison, ProRL assigns lower likelihood to these traces
supports: On shrinkage questions ProRL gives DeepSeek-R1 and Sonnet 4 traces lower likelihood than the base does.

quote: linking newly observed successes to greater likelihood of the supplied reasoning traces
supports: On expansion questions the supplied traces become more likely under ProRL.

quote: Thus, reward reweighting can expand practical access to solutions already present in the reference distribution’s tail.
supports: Idealised KL-regularised reweighting can only enlarge the accessible set: it lifts tail solutions above the resolution threshold.

quote: Exact support and the conditional distribution among correct completions remain unchanged.
supports: Under the fixed-reference binary-reward tilt, exact support and the distribution among correct completions are unchanged.

quote: zero verified successes in 8192 independent samples, the one-sided 95\% upper confidence bound on its success probability is u_{n}\approx 3.656\times 10^{-4}
supports: After 0 successes in 8,192 samples the 95 % upper bound on the per-sample success rate is 3.66e-4 (about 3/n).

quote: Verification follows each benchmark’s acceptance criterion, which may evaluate final answers without checking the intervening reasoning (Wen et al., 2025).
supports: Verification checks final answers, not the reasoning.

quote: At large sampling budgets, even infrequent false acceptances can affect observed support.
supports: The authors acknowledge that rare false acceptances can change observed support at large k.

quote: Finite sampling makes membership in the observed support set variable across repeated draws, especially for questions with rare successful responses.
supports: Membership of rare-success questions in the observed support varies across repeated draws.

quote: Our comparisons measure the outcomes of complete training recipes; identifying which components cause expansion or shrinkage requires matched interventions.
supports: The comparisons are of whole recipes; causes need matched interventions.

quote: this pattern only appears in specialized domains where base models were well-trained, and RLVR can substantially expand reasoning in other domains
supports: The paper presents ProRL's domain-dependence argument (expansion outside well-trained domains) as the opposing view.

quote: For SimpleQA, we employ GPT-4.1 as the judge.
supports: SimpleQA answers are judged by GPT-4.1; the other sets use their own checkers.

quote: the typos subset for Language tasks (LiveBench-L)
supports: LiveBench language tasks are represented only by the typos subset.

quote: RL compresses incorrect trajectories, whereas SFT expands correct ones.
supports: Headline: RL compresses incorrect trajectories; SFT expands correct ones.

quote: we also observe a reduced number of correct trajectories, explaining why Base models outperform RL models in Pass@ k at large k
supports: RL also reduces the number of distinct correct trajectories, which the authors offer as the explanation of base models winning at large k.

quote: applying RL from either Base model or SFT model dramatically reduces the number of incorrect trajectories.
supports: RL from a base model and RL from an SFT (distilled) model both cut the number of distinct incorrect trajectories.

quote: applying SFT to the Base model increases the number of correct trajectories, showing that SFT teaches new solution strategies absent in the Base model.
supports: SFT (distillation) adds correct trajectories, which the authors read as new strategies absent in the base.

quote: For each problem and model, we generate M=256 samples using a temperature of 0.6, top_p of 0.95, and a response_length of 16000.
supports: Each model writes 256 samples per problem at T 0.6, top-p 0.95, 16,000-token responses.

quote: The results for n=256 are shown in Figure 12.
supports: Pass@k is reported only to n = 256 and only in a figure.

quote: we compute pairwise similarities between the sampled outputs and apply hierarchical clustering based on thresholds.
supports: Distinct trajectories are counted by chrF similarity with threshold-cut hierarchical (UPGMA) clustering.

quote: Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B undergoes prolonged RL training for 2500 steps from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B.
supports: The analysed ProRL checkpoint is described as 2,500 RL steps from R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B (revision not stated).

quote: we maintained max_model_len=4096
supports: The Qwen2.5-Math base and Oat-Zero models are evaluated at a 4,096-token limit, the others at 16,000.

quote: AceReason-Nemotron-14B does not show performance improvement over the pre-RL DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B on the AIME25 and AMC23 domains
supports: For one SFT+RL pair (AceReason-14B on AIME25, AMC23) RL brought no accuracy gain.

quote: Finally, we confirm that Llama-3.1-8B also demonstrates squeezing of incorrect paths and expansion of correct paths following RL training.
supports: Exception: for Llama-3.1-8B, RL squeezes incorrect paths and expands correct ones.

quote: AceReason-Nemotron-1.1-7B, after SFT and RL training, expands correct paths while squeezing incorrect paths on AIME24 and AIME25.
supports: Exception: AceReason-Nemotron-1.1-7B (SFT then RL) expands correct paths on AIME24 and AIME25.

quote: Wu et al. (2025) demonstrates theoretically that RLVR cannot exceed the support of Base model.
supports: The paper cites Invisible Leash as a proof that RLVR cannot exceed the base model's support.

quote: we focused on principled algorithmic differences between RL and SFT without controlling for differences in the training datasets.
supports: RL and SFT checkpoints differ in training data, which is not controlled.

quote: For each problem, we generate M=128 samples with 7B models in Table 1
supports: The code check (HumanEval, 7B models) uses 128 samples per problem.

quote: This indicates that RL enhances Pass@ 1 through probability mass redistribution.
supports: The authors read RL's pass@1 gain as redistribution of probability mass.

quote: with models of 1.5B, 7B, and 14B parameters on mathematical and code domains
supports: Scope: 1.5B, 7B and 14B models on maths (AIME24, AIME25, AMC23) and code (HumanEval).

quote: Outcome RL raises pass@1 but not pass@k at large k (Yue et al., 2025). But every pass@1 is scored under a token budget.
supports: Premise: every pass@1 (and every training recipe) runs under a token budget, so a gain can be finishing in time.

quote: we compare the pass@1 of 20 released RL models (1.5B to 32B) with that of the thinking models they started from.
supports: The study reads 20 released outcome-RL models (1.5B-32B) against the thinking bases they started from.

quote: the five bases (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B and 7B, Qwen3-1.7B and 4B in thinking mode, OpenMath-Nemotron-1.5B)
supports: The bases are thinking (distilled or SFT) models; R1-Distill 14B and 32B bases were added later.

quote: Finishing measures answering before the budget runs out. Reliability measures being right once finished.
supports: The pass@1 change is split into finishing (answering within the budget) and reliability (right once finished), plus reach.

quote: Reach measures problems RL solves that its base answered wrongly in all eight tries, minus problems the base solves that RL answered wrongly
supports: Reach counts RL-only solves at k = 8 net of the mirror (base-only solves).

quote: We count a gain as new knowledge only when the base finishes all eight samples on the problem and gets every one wrong.
supports: A gain counts as new knowledge only if the base finished all eight samples and got all eight wrong.

quote: Reach therefore subtracts the mirror: what the base scores on the problems the RL model leaves unsolved.
supports: Reach subtracts the base's score on the problems the RL model leaves unsolved (a symmetric control for chance).

quote: Requiring all k to finish rules out problems lost only to the budget.
supports: A problem counts as unsolved only if every sample finished, so budget losses are not counted as reach.

quote: Each model writes k = 8 answers per problem at temperature T = 0.6.
supports: Each model writes eight answers per problem at T 0.6.

quote: The released pairs are read with eight samples per problem (32 or 64 on lone-win problems).
supports: The largest k is 64, used only on lone-win problems; the main reads are at k = 8.

quote: We registered predictions for ten pairs at 4k and 8k, committing them before any of their outputs existed.
supports: Predictions for ten pairs at 4k and 8k were registered before any outputs existed (cap reads were not).

quote: Where the base often hits the token budget before answering, most of the change, gain or loss, is finishing (82% at 4k and 8k).
supports: Where the base often runs out of tokens, finishing carries 82 % of the change at 4k and 8k.

quote: Given more tokens, the base closes most of the finishing gap itself.
supports: With a larger budget the base closes most of the finishing gap itself.

quote: Where the base has enough tokens, the gain is reliability: the RL model is graded right more often, even on problems both finish.
supports: Where the base finishes, the gain is reliability, including on problems both models finish.

quote: RL rarely solves what its base cannot. Reach adds at most 2.1 percentage points on any of our four physics and math sets.
supports: Net reach is at most 2.1 percentage points on each of the four physics and maths sets.

quote: We checked 144 physics problems that only the RL model solved. Of these, 3.5% hold up when resampled or read.
supports: Of 144 physics lone wins checked by resampling or reading, 3.5 % (5) hold up.

quote: In a random sample, nine of ten new RL steps a human confirmed also appear in the base’s samples.
supports: Nine of ten human-upheld 'new' RL steps also appear in the base's own samples.

quote: On four bases at 16k, the base solves 87 of RL’s 121 lone wins in 56 more samples (Table 4).
supports: With 56 extra samples the base solves 87 of 121 RL lone wins at 16k.

quote: Of what RL solves on physics, its base already solves 85%.
supports: The base already solves 85 % of what the RL model solves on physics (k = 8, 16k).

quote: The RL models solve at least one on 23% of these problems, the bases on 27%.
supports: Given 24 more samples, each side recovers a similar share of the other's lone wins (RL 23 %, base 27 %).

quote: A lone win can be chance. Eight samples can miss a problem a model solves with low probability.
supports: Lone wins at k = 8 can be sampling chance.

quote: Of 26 robust cells read, about three fifths are answer form, such as 0.000225 g against 0.225 mg.
supports: About three fifths of 26 robust reach cells read are answer-form artifacts of the matcher.

quote: No cell is a physics fact every base lacks.
supports: No robust reach cell is a physics fact absent from every base.

quote: Of the 195 wins, 42 are grading or answer-form artifacts (full table in the released repository).
supports: In the unblinded trace reading, 42 of 195 RL wins are grading or answer-form artifacts.

quote: Six of the 32B recipe’s nine robust wins on physics are answer form.
supports: For the 32B pair (Skywork-OR1-32B), six of nine robust physics wins are answer form.

quote: A more lenient answer judge removes most of the 32B recipe’s net reach.
supports: A more lenient judge removes most of the 32B recipe's net reach.

quote: 32B at its cap: gain / reliability +0.052 / +0.047
supports: At its cap the 32B recipe gains +0.052 pass@1, +0.047 of it reliability.

quote: The reach it showed at 0.6 was sampling noise and answer form.
supports: Re-read at the authors' temperature, the 32B recipe's net reach falls to about zero.

quote: The answer matcher is strict, and stricter for larger models.
supports: The answer matcher is strict, more so for larger models.

quote: Part of the measured reliability gain therefore reflects which answer forms the matcher accepts.
supports: Part of the reliability gain reflects which answer forms the matcher accepts.

quote: 3–6% of the matcher-rejected physics answers become right for the 1.5B and 1.7B models, and 10–17% for the 4B to 32B models
supports: A judge regrade turns 3-6 % (small models) and 10-17 % (4B-32B) of matcher-rejected physics answers right.

quote: Closed models were trace readers (Claude Opus 5.5) and setup grader (Claude Sonnet 5).
supports: Trace reading is by Claude Opus 5.5; setup grading by Claude Sonnet 5.

quote: One author checked the model’s claimed new steps. No human checked the step checks’ finds.
supports: Human checking is one author on the claimed new steps; the step checks' finds were not human-checked.

quote: None of the 26 steps judged decisive on the other 28 is missing from the base (Table 2).
supports: On reliability problems, every decisive RL step (26) is also in the base's samples.

quote: The base’s own wrong samples state the step too, but on 17 of the 26 they do not carry it through.
supports: The base's wrong samples state the decisive step on all 26 problems but fail to carry it through on 17.

quote: Of 120 typed misses, 41.7% are setup or concept and 1.7% computation.
supports: In the controlled run, setup or concept errors are the largest failure type (41.7 % of 120 misses).

quote: Physics is at most about 1% of the RL training data of every recipe that states its mix, except ProRL v2
supports: Physics is out of domain (at most about 1 % of stated RL data) for every recipe except ProRL v2.

quote: 136k: math, code, STEM, puzzles, instruction following
supports: ProRL v2's RL data (136k) includes instruction following.

quote: Net reach is −0.002 to +0.021, clear of zero for nine pairs and touching or straddling zero for eleven.
supports: On 276 in-domain competition-maths problems net reach is -0.002 to +0.021.

quote: Net reach at the cap is −0.006 to +0.018, clear of zero for seven pairs, touching zero for four and below zero for one.
supports: On the harder, unfiltered physics set net reach is -0.006 to +0.018.

quote: Read one by one, 13 of their 19 robust wins there stand, and none is answer form (Appendix A.6).
supports: QuestA's and KnowRL's robust wins on the harder set mostly stand when read (13 of 19).

quote: ProRL v2 R1-1.5B, cap 8k, base finishes 45%
supports: At ProRL v2's 8k training cap its base finishes 45 % of physics derivations.

quote: For ProRL v2 and e3 on physics, finishing is the whole gain (Table 7).
supports: For ProRL v2 on physics, the whole gain is finishing.

quote: Counted as unsolved, Z would raise ProRL v2’s net reach from 0.001 to 0.067
supports: Counting problems the base never solves but leaves partly unfinished as unsolved would raise ProRL v2's net reach from 0.001 to 0.067.

supports: On those partly unfinished problems, a 64k budget lets the bases solve under half of RL's wins.

supports: The authors argue the base's extra tokens are hesitation rather than missing derivation.

supports: The authors concede finishing and knowledge are not fully separable.

supports: The one zero-RL contrast pair (Open-Reasoner-Zero-7B vs Qwen2.5-7B) lengthens and finishes less at a tight budget.

quote: Models that answer in a few hundred tokens are out of scope, except one pair read for contrast
supports: Non-thinking bases are out of scope except one contrast pair.

supports: The study targets thinking bases, a case Yue et al. left open.

supports: Whether real reach grows with model scale is left open.

supports: Verdict: on the released models RL's gain is changed behaviour, not new knowledge.

supports: All pairs are read at T 0.6 although nine recipes report at 0.7-1.4 (eight re-read at authors' settings).

quote: We did not check our problems against any recipe’s training set.

supports: The controlled probe (Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, GSPO) runs at most 60 updates at a 12k cap with one seed per treated arm.

quote: In a small-scale RL run on an 8B model, the gain on new problems is finishing, with reliability flat.

supports: A lenient LLM judge of written setups was gamed (75 % vs 34 % under a strict grader).

quote: Compare a recipe with its base at or above its training cap.
supports: Recommendation: compare a recipe with its base at or above the recipe's training cap.

quote: Prolonged training is untested. Supervised distillation at scale, known to transfer (Yue et al., 2025), is untested too.
supports: The probe does not test prolonged training or large-scale distillation.

quote: Because pass@k estimates at adjacent k reuse the same generations and are nearly collinear, pointwise error bars cannot establish a sign change.
supports: A pass@k crossover is a joint claim over k; pointwise error bars cannot establish it.

quote: Across nine public RLVR checkpoints at standard 3k–16k token limits, only one narrowly meets this criterion before multiplicity adjustment
supports: Of nine public RLVR checkpoints at 3k-16k token limits, only one narrowly meets the paired crossover criterion, before multiplicity adjustment.

quote: per-response token limits alone can create, mask, or reverse a crossover through asymmetric truncation
supports: The per-response token limit alone can create, mask or reverse a crossover through asymmetric truncation.

quote: two 1.5B models exhibit certified crossovers around k ≈ 10–60, whereas two 7B models show no supported loss
supports: At 32k on 1,060 deduplicated problems, two 1.5B models (DeepScaleR, ProRL) cross with statistical support; two 7B models do not.

quote: the R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B base model truncates 30.6% of its generations, compared with 12.2% for DeepScaleR and 2.0% for ProRL
supports: At an 8k limit the base truncates 30.6 % of generations against 12.2 % (DeepScaleR) and 2.0 % (ProRL).

quote: roughly 0.7 log-odds of ProRL’s apparent pass@1 advantage at 8k was simply the base model running out of tokens
supports: About 0.7 log-odds of ProRL's 8k pass@1 advantage is the base running out of tokens.

quote: Consequently, the token limit is an integral part of the pass@k estimand.
supports: The token limit is part of the pass@k estimand.

quote: Only Qwen2.5-7B narrowly clears the per-pair band threshold before multiplicity adjustment
supports: Of the four SimpleRL-Zoo pairs used as Yue et al.'s sharpening exhibits, only Qwen2.5-7B narrowly meets the crossing criterion.

quote: its base model fails to terminate on 78% of generations
supports: On Qwen2.5-1.5B the zero-RL model stays ahead at all k <= 128 because its base fails to terminate on 78 % of generations.

quote: A pass@k crossover is therefore a property of specific checkpoints and training regimes under a stated evaluation protocol, not a universal law of long-chain RLVR.
supports: Crossovers are properties of specific checkpoints and protocols, not a universal law.
ProRL-1.5B at 32k on 1,060 new problems: D(1) +.114, D(128) -.021, certified crossover with first loss in k 12-63.

quote: AceReason-Nemotron-7B stays ahead of its R1-Distill-Qwen-7B base at every budget k ≤ 128
supports: AceReason-Nemotron-7B stays ahead of its base at every k <= 128 at 32k.

quote: DeepScaleR’s crossover remains statistically supported even if up to 83% of failed base truncations are relabeled as successes
supports: DeepScaleR's 32k crossover survives relabelling up to 83 % of failed base truncations as successes.

quote: Adding prompts (m) raises power much more than adding generations per prompt (n).
supports: For a fixed sampling budget, more prompts buy more power than deeper sampling per prompt.

quote: At m = 1000 and n = 256, ProRL-16k has only .21 dominance-test power and .14 crossing-criterion power, making non-rejection the modal outcome
supports: At 1,000 prompts x 256 samples the ProRL-16k comparison has only .21 power, so non-rejection is the modal outcome.

quote: a small minority (2%–3%) of base-solved prompts are locked into repeating an incorrect modal answer
supports: The late-k loss comes from 2-3 % of base-solved prompts locked onto a repeated wrong answer; the average prompt improves.

quote: 99.1%–99.9% of locked generations terminate naturally with a well-formed \boxed{} answer (0 verifier misses across 4,224 completions)
supports: Locked prompts are not truncation or format failures: almost all locked generations end in a well-formed boxed answer.

quote: Even under 4,352 draws per prompt (including 2,048 draws at top-p = 1.0), 13 of ProRL-16k’s 22 locked prompts remain at 0/4,352 successes.
supports: With 4,352 draws per prompt, 13 of 22 ProRL locked prompts stay at zero successes.

quote: cross below the base model between k = 178 and k = 234 and stay negative all the way to k = 4096
supports: In controlled runs from Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, all four GRPO arms fall behind the base at k 178-234 and stay behind to k = 4,096.

quote: whereas SFT stays significantly ahead at every budget
supports: The SFT arm stays significantly ahead of the base at every budget to k = 4,096.

quote: can reliably diagnose behavior up to k ≈ n, but claims at k ≫ n require sampling at those budgets
supports: Claims at k much larger than the sampling depth n need sampling at those budgets; extrapolation loses sign resolution.

quote: our controlled GRPO and SFT runs use 100–132 updates on a 1.5B base model (17 to 30 times fewer steps than DeepScaleR or ProRL)
supports: The controlled runs are short (100-132 updates) relative to the public recipes.

quote: Dragoi et al. (2025) note that random guessing creates an artificial floor at k ∼ 1/pguess (which our free-form symbolic and execution verifiers avoid)
supports: Random guessing creates a pass@k floor at k ~ 1/p_guess; the paper's free-form answers avoid it.

quote: Always report per-response token limits and truncation rates for both models, and verify whether raising the token limit alters the comparison.
supports: Recommendation: report truncation rates for both models and test token-limit sensitivity.

quote: decoded throughout at temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95 with symbolic-equivalence verification via Math-Verify
supports: Decoding T 0.6, top-p 0.95; grading by Math-Verify symbolic equivalence, identical for both sides.

quote: strictly deduplicated against DeepScaleR’s training set and every other prompt set in this study
supports: The clean benchmark is deduplicated against training data and all other prompt sets.

quote: RLVR disproportionately reinforces problems with high likelihood, correct solutions, under the base model, while suppressing other initially low-likelihood ones.
supports: Winner-take-all: RLVR reinforces problems whose correct solutions are already likely and suppresses low-likelihood ones.

quote: This work provides concrete evidence that LLMs can acquire genuinely new skills during RL by composing existing ones
supports: In a synthetic string-function task, RL teaches unseen compositions of known skills.

quote: it synthesizes new composite strategies only when the base model has first mastered the independent atomic skills via SFT
supports: RL synthesizes new composite strategies only once the atomic skills are mastered.

quote: RLVR incentivizes the exploration of previously inaccessible solution paths by amplifying the model's existing skills
supports: Sharpening atomic steps opens previously inaccessible multi-step paths.

quote: achieving success on problems where the base policy VLM consistently attains $0\%$ accuracy despite increasing pass@k sampling budgets
supports: On synthetic mazes, RLVR solves problems the base VLM never solves at any sampled budget.

quote: reports often conflate policy improvement with three confounds: (i) budget mismatch between RLVR and baseline evaluations, (ii) attempt inflation and calibration drift
supports: Headline RLVR gains are confounded by budget mismatch, attempt inflation and contamination.

quote: we show that RL-trained models struggle with fundamentally new problems, hitting a 'coverage wall' due to insufficient planning skills
supports: GRPO mainly improves execution; RL models hit a coverage wall on new problems.

quote: our algorithm offers substantial boosts in reasoning that nearly match and even outperform those from RL on a wide variety of single-shot tasks
supports: MCMC power sampling of the base nearly matches RL's single-shot gains without training.

quote: the analysis of Pass@k curves indicates that RL-PLUS effectively resolves the capability boundary collapse problem.
supports: A hybrid off-policy method claims to remove large-k boundary collapse.

quote: PSN-GRPO consistently expands the effective reasoning capability boundary across multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks and model families
supports: Parameter-space-noise exploration raises pass@k at large budgets (e.g. 256).

quote: scales to 32B-parameter models and sampling budgets up to $K=1024$
supports: A candidate-support method improves pass@K across K up to 1,024 and models up to 32B.

quote: we analyze the pass@k objective, derive its gradient, and demonstrate that it is fundamentally a per-example positive reweighting of the simpler pass@1 objective
supports: The pass@k objective is a per-example reweighting of pass@1 with a vanishing signal where exploration matters.

quote: when the structural advantage is not present, RLVR may converge to suboptimal compositions
supports: Theory: compositional tasks are learnable from outcome reward only when correct intermediate steps carry an advantage.

quote: clarifying how RL-only post-training induces OOD generalization beyond what standard metrics such as pass@k reveal
supports: On Countdown, RL induces compositional OOD generalisation not visible in pass@k.

quote: 3,000 steps in all, counting ProRL v1’s 2,000
supports: ProRL v2 is 3,000 RL steps in all, counting ProRL v1's 2,000.

quote: We conducted evaluations on AIME24, AIME25, and AMC23 using the same implementation as Yue et al. (2025).
supports: Pass@k grading follows Yue et al.'s implementation.

quote: R1-Distill-1.5B GRPO with KL; 50 steps
supports: The shortest recipe read (Open-RS3) ran 50 GRPO steps.

quote: entropy bonus, clip-higher; 4,380 steps
supports: The longest stated recipe (JustRL-DeepSeek) ran 4,380 steps.

quote: DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview (Luo et al., 2025) and ProRL (Liu et al., 2025), evaluated across 8k, 16k, and 32k token limits
supports: The audit includes DeepScaleR-1.5B and ProRL (from R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) at 8k, 16k and 32k limits.

quote: the four SimpleRL-Zoo checkpoints (Zeng et al., 2025) on Qwen2.5-7B, 14B, 32B (Qwen et al., 2024) and Llama-3.1-8B
supports: The audit includes the four SimpleRL-Zoo checkpoints Yue et al. used as sharpening exhibits.

quote: We track DAPO training on DeepSeek-1.5B to examine how empirical support evolves across checkpoints (Tab. 4).
supports: The only within-run trajectory is the authors' own DAPO run on R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, read every 30 steps to step 300.

quote: Misspecification of max_model_len causes substantial accuracy degradation in the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-based models, which performs lengthy reasoning.
supports: A too-short length limit (Yue et al.'s 4,096) substantially lowers pass@k of long-reasoning distilled models.
AceReason-Nemotron-14B overall: P 2,418, E 8, S 23, O 501 (losses about 1 % of base-solved questions).

quote: The set keeps only problems the controlled run’s base solves at least sometimes, so pass@1 can move.
supports: The main physics set is filtered to problems the probe's base sometimes solves, which caps measurable reach.

quote: The human check took one author one sitting of about half an hour.
supports: The human check was one author, about half an hour.

quote: One author, blind to side, checked the claimed new steps in 50 of the 143 pairs
supports: One author, blind to side, checked claimed new steps in 50 of 143 pairs.
